paras.text: Topic: 休閒 Leisure
• Use time expressions to describe events.
• Discuss travel plans with friends.
• Talk about hypothetical situations.
• Give suggestions about leisure activities.
Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue I. The book’s own Dialogue I is on book p. 182 (PDF p. 209); its recording is track 09-01.

lines.zh: 明華，這個星期我們放三天的假，你要回國嗎？
lines.py: Mínghuá, zhè ge xīngqí wǒmen fàng sān tiān de jià, nǐ yào huíguó ma?

lines.zh: 不，我打算在家看小說、聽音樂學中文，你呢？
lines.py: Bù, wǒ dǎsuàn zài jiā kàn xiǎoshuō, tīng yīnyuè xué Zhōngwén, nǐ ne?

lines.zh: 我想跟朋友出去玩。
lines.py: Wǒ xiǎng gēn péngyǒu chūqù wán.

lines.zh: 不錯啊。去什麼地方？
lines.py: Búcuò a. Qù shénme dìfāng?

lines.zh: 花蓮。聽說那裡的風景非常漂亮。
lines.py: Huālián. Tīngshuō nàlǐ de fēngjǐng fēicháng piàoliàng.

lines.zh: 我也聽說。放假的時候，你常去旅行嗎？
lines.py: Wǒ yě tīngshuō. Fàngjià de shíhòu, nǐ cháng qù lǚxíng ma?

lines.zh: 不一定。有時候在家寫功課，有時候出去玩。
lines.py: Bù yídìng. Yǒu shíhòu zài jiā xiě gōngkè, yǒu shíhòu chūqù wán.

lines.zh: 你們什麼時候去花蓮？
lines.py: Nǐmen shénme shíhòu qù Huālián?

lines.zh: 這個星期五下午去。
lines.py: Zhè ge xīngqíwǔ xiàwǔ qù.

lines.zh: 去玩多久？
lines.py: Qù wán duō jiǔ?

lines.zh: 大概玩三天。
lines.py: Dàgài wán sān tiān.

translation.en: Minghua, we have a three-day break this week. Are you going back to your country?
No, I plan to stay home, read novels, and study Chinese by listening to music. How about you?
I’d like to go out with friends.
Sounds good. Where to?
Hualien. I’ve heard the scenery there is lovely.
I’ve heard that too. Do you often travel on your days off?
Not necessarily. Sometimes I stay home to do homework, sometimes I go out.
When are you going to Hualien?
This Friday afternoon.
How long will you be there?
Probably about three days.

lines.zh: 我男朋友十月五號要來臺灣看我。
lines.py: Wǒ nánpéngyǒu shíyuè wǔ hào yào lái Táiwān kàn wǒ.

lines.zh: 你想帶他去哪裡玩？
lines.py: Nǐ xiǎng dài tā qù nǎlǐ wán?

lines.zh: 還不知道。你有什麼建議？
lines.py: Hái bù zhīdào. Nǐ yǒu shénme jiànyì?

lines.zh: 臺灣的夜市很有名。你們應該去逛逛。
lines.py: Táiwān de yèshì hěn yǒumíng. Nǐmen yīnggāi qù guàngguàng.

lines.zh: 謝謝，還有什麼好玩的地方？
lines.py: Xièxie, hái yǒu shénme hǎowán de dìfāng?

lines.zh: 臺灣的咖啡也很特別。臺北有很多咖啡店。
lines.py: Táiwān de kāfēi yě hěn tèbié. Táiběi yǒu hěn duō kāfēi diàn.

lines.zh: 到哪裡喝咖啡比較好？
lines.py: Dào nǎlǐ hē kāfēi bǐjiào hǎo?

lines.zh: 你們可以去貓空。那裡的風景很美。
lines.py: Nǐmen kěyǐ qù Māokōng. Nàlǐ de fēngjǐng hěn měi.

lines.zh: 謝謝你。我決定帶他去貓空。你也一起去，好不好？
lines.py: Xièxie nǐ. Wǒ juédìng dài tā qù Māokōng. Nǐ yě yìqǐ qù, hǎo bù hǎo?

lines.zh: 要是那時候我有空，就跟你們一起去。
lines.py: Yàoshì nà shíhòu wǒ yǒu kòng, jiù gēn nǐmen yìqǐ qù.

lines.zh: 太好了！謝謝！
lines.py: Tài hǎo le! Xièxie!

translation.en: My boyfriend is coming to Taiwan to see me on October 5th.
Where do you want to take him?
I don’t know yet. Any suggestions?
Taiwan’s night markets are famous. You two should go have a look around.
Thanks. What other fun places are there?
Taiwanese coffee is special too. Taipei has lots of coffee shops.
Where’s a good place to have coffee?
You could go to Maokong. The scenery there is beautiful.
Thanks. I’ve decided to take him to Maokong. Why don’t you come along too?
If I’m free at that time, I’ll go with you.
Great! Thank you!

paras.text: Use: A time-when phrase says when something happens — a point on the calendar or clock (去年, 這個星期, 昨天, 六點). A time-duration phrase says how long something lasts — a stretch of time (一年, 這個星期要上五天的課, 半個鐘頭). The two expressions often look alike but are not interchangeable.

head: Time-When
Time-Duration
rows: 一年、兩年… ／ 半年、一年半
一個月、兩個月… ／ 半個月、一個半月
一天、兩天… ／ 半天、一天半
一個鐘頭、兩個鐘頭… ／ 半個鐘頭

items.zh: 我下個星期要去花蓮玩。
items.py: Wǒ xià ge xīngqí yào qù Huālián wán.
items.en: I’m going to Hualien next week. (time-when)

items.zh: 我想在花蓮玩一個星期。
items.py: Wǒ xiǎng zài Huālián wán yí ge xīngqí.
items.en: I’d like to spend a week in Hualien. (time-duration)
He went back to his country yesterday. (time-when)

items.zh: 這個電影要看三個鐘頭。
items.py: Zhè ge diànyǐng yào kàn sān ge zhōngtóu.
items.en: This movie takes three hours to watch. (time-duration)

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Decide whether each blank needs a time-when or a time-duration phrase, then fill it in.

items.prompt: 我想學中文學＿＿＿＿＿＿（a year and a half）。

blocks.en: II. Time-Duration: how long an action lasts

paras.text: Use: A duration phrase answers “for how long”. It follows the verb directly: Subject + Verb + Duration.
If the verb has an object, the verb must be repeated: Subject + Verb + Object + Verb + Duration.
A duration phrase comes before the negative word, not after it: Subject + Duration + 不／沒 + Verb.
If the verb is a separable verb (放假, 上課…), the duration is inserted inside it, with or without 的: 放三天的假 or 放假放三天.

items.zh: 我想去花蓮玩一個星期。
items.py: Wǒ xiǎng qù Huālián wán yí ge xīngqí.
items.en: I’d like to go play in Hualien for a week.

items.py: Zhōngwén, wǒ xiǎng xué yì nián bàn.
items.en: Chinese — I’d like to study it for a year and a half.

items.py: Tā dǎsuàn jiāo Zhōngwén jiāo yì nián.
items.en: He plans to teach Chinese for a year.

items.zh: 我每個星期學書法學兩天。
items.py: Wǒ měi ge xīngqí xué shūfǎ xué liǎng tiān.
items.en: I study calligraphy two days every week.

items.zh: 學校下個月放三天的假。
items.py: Xuéxiào xià ge yuè fàng sān tiān de jià.
items.en: The school is giving three days off next month.

items.zh: 他太忙了，所以兩天不能來上課。
items.py: Tā tài máng le, suǒyǐ liǎng tiān bù néng lái shàngkè.
items.en: He’s too busy, so he can’t come to class for two days.

items.zh: 這裡沒有網路，所以我兩個星期不能上網。
items.py: Zhèlǐ méi yǒu wǎnglù, suǒyǐ wǒ liǎng ge xīngqí bù néng shàngwǎng.
items.en: There’s no internet here, so I can’t go online for two weeks.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Make a sentence with the verb + duration pattern.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Use 動詞+時段 to describe each part of Antong’s day: 11:00–12:30 上網 (1.5 hrs), 15:00–16:00 教弟弟功課 (1 hr), 17:00–17:30 游泳 (半個鐘頭).

items.prompt: 他早上十一點到十二點半＿＿＿＿＿＿。

paras.text: Use: A clause ending in 的時候 names the time something else happens, happened, or will happen — like an English “when” clause. The 的時候 clause usually comes first, and the main clause follows.

items.zh: 在山上看風景的時候，我覺得很舒服。
items.py: Zài shānshàng kàn fēngjǐng de shíhòu, wǒ juéde hěn shūfú.
items.en: When I was looking at the scenery in the mountains, I felt great.

items.zh: 放假的時候，我喜歡去逛夜市。
items.py: Fàngjià de shíhòu, wǒ xǐhuān qù guàng yèshì.
items.en: On days off, I like to wander around the night market.

items.zh: 你有空的時候，請到我家來玩。
items.py: Nǐ yǒu kòng de shíhòu, qǐng dào wǒ jiā lái wán.
items.en: When you’re free, please come over to my place.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Answer each question with a 的時候 clause.

items.prompt: 你不上課的時候，常做什麼？→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
你有空的時候，喜歡做什麼？→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
你在圖書館的時候，常做什麼？→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: IV. 有時候 yǒu shíhòu …，有時候 yǒu shíhòu …: sometimes … and sometimes …

paras.text: Use: This pattern names two things that alternate within the same situation — “sometimes A, sometimes B”.

items.zh: 我有時候吃中國菜，有時候吃越南菜。
items.py: Wǒ yǒu shíhòu chī Zhōngguó cài, yǒu shíhòu chī Yuènán cài.
items.en: Sometimes I eat Chinese food, sometimes Vietnamese food.

items.zh: 在圖書館的時候，我有時候看書，有時候上網。
items.py: Zài túshūguǎn de shíhòu, wǒ yǒu shíhòu kànshū, yǒu shíhòu shàngwǎng.
items.en: In the library, I sometimes read, sometimes go online.

items.zh: 放假的時候，我有時候在家寫功課，有時候出去玩。
items.py: Fàngjià de shíhòu, wǒ yǒu shíhòu zài jiā xiě gōngkè, yǒu shíhòu chūqù wán.
items.en: On days off, sometimes I stay home and do homework, sometimes I go out.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete with 有時候…有時候….

items.prompt: 你在餐廳吃飯的時候，常點什麼？→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
你放假的時候，常去哪裡？→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: V. 要是 yàoshì … 就 jiù …: condition and consequence

paras.text: Use: 要是 introduces a condition (“if …”), and 就 in the second clause introduces the result (“then …”). 要是 may stand before or after the subject of the first clause; 就 always comes right at the start of the second clause’s predicate (after its subject, if there is one).

items.zh: 你要是星期日有空，你就跟我去旅行吧！
items.py: Nǐ yàoshì xīngqírì yǒu kòng, nǐ jiù gēn wǒ qù lǚxíng ba!
items.en: If you’re free on Sunday, come travel with me!

items.zh: 要是下個月不忙，她就回國。
items.py: Yàoshì xià ge yuè bù máng, tā jiù huíguó.
items.en: If she isn’t busy next month, she’ll go back to her country.

items.zh: 要是我有空，我就跟朋友一起去KTV唱歌。
items.py: Yàoshì wǒ yǒu kòng, wǒ jiù gēn péngyǒu yìqǐ qù KTV chànggē.
items.en: If I’m free, I’ll go sing at KTV with friends.

items.zh: 你要是沒空，我們就不要去逛夜市。
items.py: Nǐ yàoshì méi kòng, wǒmen jiù bú yào qù guàng yèshì.
items.en: If you’re not free, let’s not go to the night market.

items.zh: 要是他不喜歡喝咖啡，就不要帶他去咖啡店。
items.py: Yàoshì tā bù xǐhuān hē kāfēi, jiù bú yào dài tā qù kāfēi diàn.
items.en: If he doesn’t like coffee, don’t take him to a coffee shop.

blocks.en: I. How Much Time Is Spent?

paras.text: Goal: Use time expressions to describe events.
Task: Look at a short piece of information for each question below and answer with the right time-when or time-duration phrase.
1. 田中想去花蓮玩幾天？（4月3日到4月10日）
2. 安同打算在臺灣學多久的中文？（2013年到2018年）
3. 月美跟臺灣朋友打算去貓空玩多久？（下午兩點到四點）
4. 如玉的爸媽決定在臺灣旅行多久？（4月6日到4月11日）
Goal: Talk about hypothetical situations, using 要是…就….
Task: Your partner says they don’t like or don’t want to do something. Suggest an alternative with 要是…就…, e.g. 要是你不喜歡喝咖啡，就喝茶。 Then swap roles for each of: 不要去游泳、不想打網球、不喜歡看電視、不去圖書館、覺得打籃球沒意思.
Goal: Discuss travel plans with friends.

Task 1: Imagine a friend’s travel schedule (e.g. train to Hualien on Friday afternoon, visiting Taroko Gorge on Saturday, trying local snacks, and taking the train back on Sunday morning) and tell the class about it, using time-when and time-duration expressions.

Task 2: Pair up and ask a partner about their plans for the next break — where, with whom, how they’re getting there, and for how long. Note the answers in a table, then compare with the class which destination is the most popular.

Nearly every television program in Taiwan — except live news — runs with Chinese subtitles that cannot be turned off, and viewers are used to watching with them on. A few things are usually given as reasons for this.

One is that subtitles let people who are hard of hearing follow along. Another is that spoken Mandarin varies a good deal by region and accent, and by the other Chinese languages and dialects spoken across Taiwan, while the written characters stay the same; subtitles make programs easier to follow regardless of accent. A third reason has to do with tones: Chinese is a tonal language, and in connected speech those tones can shift and blend, so a string of sounds can be heard more than one way. The classic example is 基隆是雨港 Jīlóng shì yǔgǎng “Keelung is a rainy port”, which without subtitles could easily be misheard as 基隆是漁港 Jīlóng shì yúgǎng “Keelung is a fishing port” — seeing the characters removes the ambiguity.

Because Chinese characters are not an alphabet and the link between a written word and its sound is looser than in an alphabetic language, seeing the text alongside hearing it makes spoken Chinese noticeably easier to follow — which is part of why subtitles have become the norm.
